name: Wallow Loop
waypoints: 0.0~South Gate spur joins the loop|0.4~Warming Hut and the south shore|0.7~Pond willow and the outflow|0.9~Bald cypress at the outflow|1.1~The Wallow Boathouse|1.4~Tanner's Run inlet and boardwalk|1.6~Back at the spur
summary: A flat, paved loop around the Wallow, the park's lake. The most walked mile and a half in the city.
body:
The loop is step-free all the way round, with a bench every 300 feet and lighting until the park closes at 11:00 pm.

Runners go counterclockwise; walkers either way.

name: Ridge Trail
surface: Natural surface, roots and rock steps
waypoints: 0.0~North Gate trailhead|0.6~First switchbacks|1.0~Lightning tuliptree|1.2~Hillcrest Overlook, 742 ft|1.6~Hillcrest beech|2.1~Down through the oaks|2.4~Joins the Wallow Loop at Tanner's Run
summary: The park's only real climb: from the North Gate up through Cadwallow Woods to Hillcrest Overlook, then down to the Wallow.
body:
Roots and rock steps make this the hardest trail in the park. After rain the switchbacks below the overlook stay slick for a day or two.

The trail closes at dusk: there are no lights in the woods.

name: Tanner's Run Trail
dogs: On a leash (not on the boardwalk blinds)
waypoints: 0.0~Creek footbridge near the North Gate|0.3~Old tannery foundations|0.6~Tanner's sycamore|0.8~Boardwalk and bird blinds|1.1~The Wallow inlet
summary: Follows Tanner's Run from the woods down to the Wallow, ending on the boardwalk over the wetland.
body: The gravel section is step-free; the older part of the boardwalk has a step at each end until the replacement is finished.

name: Meadow Path
dogs: On a leash; off-leash hours 6–9 am in the kite field
waypoints: 0.0~West Gate|0.3~Council Oak|0.6~Native meadow plots|0.9~Linden Shelter|1.3~Back at the West Gate
summary: A loop around the Long Meadow, past the Council Oak and the native meadow plots.
body: Mown wide enough for a wheelchair in dry weather; the crushed stone section by the Linden Shelter is firm all year.

name: Perimeter Path
waypoints: 0.0~South Gate|0.9~West Gate and the bike path|1.7~North Gate|2.5~Walled Garden|3.0~East Gate|3.6~Elm Walk Shelter|4.2~Back at the South Gate
summary: The paved path around the edge of the park, shared by walkers, runners and cyclists.
body: Cyclists keep right and ride at walking pace near the gates. The path is plowed first after snow.
